'''Papa Ababacar Bartolome Miller''' (born February 7, 2004) is a Spanish [[college basketball]] player for the [[Cincinnati Bearcats men's basketball|Cincinnati Bearcats]] of the [[Big 12 Conference]]. He previously played for the [[Florida State Seminoles men's basketball|Florida State Seminoles]] and [[Florida Atlantic Owls men's basketball|Florida Atlantic Owls]].

== Early life ==
Miller was born on February 7, 2004, in [[Mallorca]], one of the [[Balearic Islands]] in Spain.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/player/_/id/5075626/baba-miller|publisher=[[ESPN]]|title=Baba Miller}}</ref><ref name="auto">{{Cite web|url=https://seminoles.com/sports/mens-basketball/roster/baba-miller/6480|publisher=[[Florida State Seminoles]]|title=Baba Miller}}</ref> He has British ancestry.<ref name="auto2">{{Cite news|url=https://en.as.com/ncaa/real-madrid-lose-youth-team-pearl-baba-miller-to-florida-state-n/|newspaper=[[Diario AS]]|title=Real Madrid lose youth team pearl Baba Miller to Florida State|date=June 12, 2022|author=Maestre, Mike; Hall, Andy}}</ref> He began playing as a youth for [[CB Bahía San Agustín]] of Mallorca and later moved to [[Madrid]] to play for [[Distrito Olímpico]].<ref name="auto2"/> At age 12, he joined [[Real Madrid Baloncesto]] and played with the organization through the 2021–22 season.<ref name="auto1">{{Cite web|url=https://www.si.com/college/wake-forest/basketball/baba-miller-florida-states-mystery-freshman|website=[[Sports Illustrated]]|title=Baba Miller: Florida State's Mystery Freshman|date=January 11, 2023|author=Conroy, Ben}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.tallahassee.com/story/sports/college/fsu/mensbasketball/2022/06/06/fsu-basketball-lands-commitment-real-madrid-forward-baba-miller/7532620001/|newspaper=[[Tallahassee Democrat]]|title=Florida State men's basketball lands pledge from top international prospect Baba Miller|date=June 6, 2022|author=Karels, Carter}}</ref> Starting with the youth B team, he played through all the team categories and was promoted to the senior team in December 2021, making his [[EuroLeague]] debut in a 71–65 win over [[PBC CSKA Moscow]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.gigantes.com/liga-endesa/baba-miller/|website=Gigantes.com|title=El canterano Baba Miller, inscrito por el Real Madrid para el partido ante el CSKA. Así juega la perla de la cantera blanca (vídeo)|date=December 22, 2021|language=Spanish}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.cope.es/emisoras/illes-balears/baleares/mallorca/deportes-mallorca/noticias/baba-miller-debuta-con-primer-equipo-del-real-madrid-euroliga-20211224_1696779|website=[[COPE (website)|COPE]]|title=Baba Miller debuta con el primer equipo del Real Madrid en la Euroliga|date=December 24, 2021|language=Spanish|author=Jiménez, Jordi}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.marca.com/en/basketball/nba/2023/01/11/63be8960ca4741db158b457c.html|newspaper=[[Marca (newspaper)|Marca]]|title=Baba Miller: The enigmatic Spaniard who is ranked Top-10 in the NBA Draft without having made NCAA debut|date=November 1, 2022|author=Corbella, Enrique}}</ref> He was a member of Real Madrid's winning team in the [[2020–21 Euroleague Basketball Next Generation Tournament]] and averaged 11.3 points and 5.3 rebounds per game with the [[Real Madrid Baloncesto B|Real Madrid B Team]] in 2021–22.<ref name="auto2"/><ref name="auto1"/><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.si.com/nba/draft/prospect-profiles/nba-draft-scouting-report-florida-states-baba-miller#gid=ci02aa0481f00025c7&pid=usatsi_20165808|website=[[Sports Illustrated]]|title=NBA Draft Scouting Report: Florida State's Baba Miller|date=August 30, 2022}}</ref>

== College career ==
Miller decided to move to the United States and play for a team in the [[National Collegiate Athletic Association]] (NCAA) in 2022, stating that he thought it was best for his development.<ref name="auto2"/> Considered one of the top international prospects, he committed to play for the [[Florida State Seminoles men's basketball|Florida State Seminoles]] over the [[Gonzaga Bulldogs men's basketball|Gonzaga Bulldogs]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.si.com/college/gonzaga/basketball/miller-commits-to-fsu|website=[[Sports Illustrated]]|title=It's Florida State over Gonzaga for Spanish prospect Baba Miller|author=Ali, Asher|date=June 6, 2022}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/story/_/id/34047241/top-international-basketball-prospect-baba-miller-commits-florida-state-seminoles|publisher=[[ESPN]]|title=Top international basketball prospect Baba Miller commits to Florida State Seminoles|author=Givony, Jonathan|date=June 6, 2022}}</ref> Prior to the start of the season, Miller was suspended by the NCAA, initially for the entire year but later for 16 games, due to him having received [[US$]] 3,000 in third-party money to attend a training camp in 2020; his family paid the money back once they learned that it violated NCAA rules, but the suspension was upheld, drawing widespread criticism.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.si.com/college/fsu/basketball/the-ncaas-last-stand-detailing-the-unjust-suspension-of-baba-miller|website=[[Sports Illustrated]]|title=The NCAA's Last Stand: detailing the unjust suspension of Baba Miller|author=Veazey, Austin|date=November 3, 2022}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.tallahassee.com/story/sports/college/fsu/mensbasketball/2022/11/05/fsu-coach-leonard-hamilton-baba-miller-situation-we-going-move-on/10648662002/|newspaper=[[Tallahassee Democrat]]|title=Florida State men's basketball: Leonard Hamilton assesses Baba Miller situation, team before season|author=Karels, Carter|date=November 5, 2022}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.newspapers.com/article/the-stuart-news/135903579/|newspaper=[[The Stuart News]]|via=[[Newspapers.com]]|date=January 11, 2023|page=C5|title=Freshman Miller to make debut for FSU at Wake Forest|author=Kassim, Ehsan}} {{Open access}}</ref> He made his return from suspension against the [[Wake Forest Demon Deacons men's basketball|Wake Forest Demon Deacons]], scoring four points and having four rebounds in a 90–75 loss.<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://en.as.com/ncaa/baba-miller-makes-ncaa-debut-after-lengthy-suspension-n/|newspaper=[[Diario AS]]|title=Baba Miller makes NCAA debut after lengthy suspension|date=January 12, 2023}}</ref> He finished the season with 15 games played while averaging 4.3 points and 3.7 rebounds per game.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://floridastate.rivals.com/news/baba-miller-plans-return-to-fsu|website=[[Rivals.com]]|title=Baba Miller wants to 'try to make things right' at FSU in return|date=April 14, 2023}}</ref>

Miller announced in April 2023 that he was returning for his [[sophomore]] season at Florida State rather than declaring for the [[2023 NBA draft]].<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.tallahassee.com/story/sports/college/fsu/mensbasketball/2023/04/14/fsu-mens-basketball-baba-miller-plans-to-return-to-seminoles/70115479007/|newspaper=[[Tallahassee Democrat]]|title=Forward Baba Miller plans to return to Florida State men's basketball for sophomore season|author=Kassim, Ehsan|date=April 14, 2023}}</ref>

In May 2024, Miller announced he was withdrawing from the NBA draft and that he would be transferring to Florida Atlantic University.

== International career ==
Miller played for the [[Spain men's national under-18 basketball team]], including at the [[2021 FIBA U18 European Challengers]] tournament where he averaged 11.8 points, 4.4 rebounds and 2.0 assists per game.<ref name="auto"/> In 2023, he was a member of the [[Spain men's national under-19 basketball team|national under-19 team]] that won the [[2023 FIBA Under-19 Basketball World Cup|FIBA Under-19 Basketball World Cup]], starting in the finals and recording 11 points scored and five rebounds in the game, while having an average of 9.4 points and 6.0 rebounds in the tournament.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://floridastate.rivals.com/news/baba-miller-enjoys-gold-medal-run-experience-earned-with-spanish-team|website=[[Rivals.com]]|title=Baba Miller enjoys gold medal run, experience earned with Spanish team|date=July 11, 2023|author=Ferrante, Bob}}</ref>
